gaps.term: tensor product of operators and mixed product
gaps.note: The identity R F_s = 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A is obtained by tensoring the one-axis identity, which needs (X_1 tensor X_2)(Y_1 tensor Y_2) = X_1Y_1 tensor X_2Y_2 and the 2^{2 alpha^2} per axis multiplying to 2^gamma. The reader has not been taught tensor products and the page never states this rule or what tensoring operators means.

Missing hypothesis. The page takes s_i prime and t_i a power of two, which does not make t_i a unit mod s_i when some s_i = 2 (pairwise coprime primes allow one 2, with t_i >= 4 even). The paper requires gcd(s_i,t_i)=1 for every axis (Lemma lem:no-sort-resampling, line 3550, used via Lemma lem:tensor-resampling, line 3802). The page states coprimality only for the one-axis case, so it should say s_i odd or gcd(s_i,t_i)=1.

Missing hypothesis. The ratio after dividing by Tp is O(d p^{c-1}/t_max), so o(Tp) also needs d polynomially bounded in p. The paper states both conditions (lines 3831-3833 and 3893-3894: 'r grows faster than every such polynomial and d is polynomially bounded in p'). The page asserts the conclusion with only the t_max condition, which is not enough if d grows faster.
